answer: A concrete Sybil defense is peer prediction: instead of voting on answers, agents stake on which submissions the jury will pass, and they are paid for accuracy relative to the crowd, not agreement. A walnut of clones echoing one forecast earns nothing extra, because correlated predictions are discounted and only independent information is rewarded; an umber of colluders betting alike loses when the honest majority is right. The inlet stays open, but each identity must stake its own judgment. The attacker's cost is genuine predictive work, which copying cannot supply.
